response: Yes, age can moderate the effect of personality disorder on coping style in psychiatric inpatients. Research suggests that older adults with personality disorders may employ more adaptive coping strategies, such as acceptance and emotional regulation, whereas younger adults may rely more on maladaptive coping mechanisms, such as avoidance or substance use. Additionally, older adults may have developed more effective coping strategies over time due to life experience, which can mitigate the impact of personality disorder on their coping style. Therefore, age can influence the relationship between personality disorder and coping style in psychiatric inpatients.
